newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares paused their record-breaking run on Tuesday, ending fractionally lower after lodging six consecutive record closing highs.
The AEX ended a largely range-bound session down 0.58 points at 609.46 after briefly touching an all-time high of 611.80 in early morning.
Dealers said firmer bonds and a strong Wall Street opening on the back of lower October housing starts had been unable to offset the weaker dollar.
"The housing starts data gave the market a nudge up, because we knew which way Wall Street would go," a dealer said.
But despite a 20 point rise in New York's Dow Jones Industrial index the AEX later gave up its gains.
Financials built on Monday's gains, with Aegon continuing its recovery after Friday's dip on third-quarter profit figures following an upbeat presentation to analysts.

ING shares spent most of the day in positive territory, but closed the session unchanged at 59.50 ahead of third-quarter results due on Thursday. Dealers said that while some investors were taking profits, others were moving in to take their place.

Brewer Heineken again booked some of the day's heaviest losses, giving up 4.40 or 1.71 percent to 281.10. Dealers said it was losing its growth stock image. One said the brewer lacked the managers to keep up with its acquisitions strategy.
Another said the stock was still feeling the effects of a recent broker downgrade.
Philips added 1.20 guilders to 63.60, buoyed by news it plans to launch a hand-held personal computer. The so-called HPC was presented in Las Vegas on Monday.

Printer and copier maker Oce van der Grinten gained a leg up from news U.S. sector rival Xerox planned to increase printer prices. The stock closed the day up 0.20 at 189.00 guilders after having opened 0.80 guilders lower.
On the national issues market, bourse newcomer Endemol Entertainment surged three guilders to 59.50.
Dealers said the television production company's announcement it will transfer its stake in loss-making television channel Sport 7 to Endemol management had gained a big welcome from investors.
"It's a very positive development," said one dealer. "We saw the stake in Sport 7 as the only cloud on the horizon for this stock."
